findings.summary: No test pairs an override at the critical level with a request past STARVATION_AGE_SECONDS, so the loop at queue_order.py:383-386 that keeps criticals behind aged work could be removed and every named test would still pass, silently restoring the starvation regression this fix was written to repair.
findings.text: The helper's docstring states two boundaries: an aged request keeps its precedence, and a queue with no review is returned unchanged. Only the second is exercised (tests/test_a_critical_request_takes_a_slot_before_reviews.py covers override 100/99/none, project level 50, the fair-share pass, and the promotion path). Because _precedence puts aged non-review rows after the reviews, removing the `if now is not None:` insert-move would place a critical request at the first review's index, ahead of every aged row, with no red test. The five restored shared-order tests do not carry an override at the critical level, so they do not close the gap.
findings.title: the starvation boundary of the new move has no test

findings.summary: priorities_first's local _critical re-expresses the rule queue_order._critical_ahead_of_reviews._is_critical now owns, and the two differ (the local one has no starvation or review guard), so a later change to one leaves the hoist and the shared order disagreeing.
findings.text: queue_order.py:363-372 decides criticality with an is_review and a _starved guard; admission/ordering.py:319-323 decides it again as `_critical_level(pointer, config_for) <= points`. The comment at ordering.py:331 claims the move is 'applied again rather than reimplemented', which is true of the move but not of the predicate. Today the divergence is inert because `raised` already excludes aged pointers and reviews, but it is the same drift class the previous review recorded at this line.
findings.title: the criticality predicate is still written twice
